page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware provisioning consists of 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or hardware GPUs are included, and networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements show high per-thread efficiency contrasted by modest aggregate throughput. In single-core testing, the instance registers strong marks, with stress-ng single-core reaching 3111.68 points to place in the top ten percent and Geekbench single-core achieving 1997.0 points in the top quartile. However, because overall compute resources are limited to 2 vCPUs on one core, multi-core metrics settle in the lower twenty-five percent across PassMark, Geekbench multi-core, and stress-ng multi-core evaluations. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks run at average levels, registering 47.32 GB/sec for uncached reads and 27.49 GB/sec for writes, whereas cached small-block bandwidth remains limited. Application-level performance reflects these characteristics, with static web serving registering 2.87 GB/sec, Redis SET reaching 2.88 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations placing in the bottom ten percent.

From an efficiency standpoint, the hardware profile offers cost-effective access to modern Zen-generation computing architectures without the overhead of auxiliary components like GPUs or local disks. The architectural tradeoff centers on low aggregate thread count and compact memory capacity, which inherently constrain parallel execution and memory-heavy operations. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large fits environments requiring dedicated execution threads for single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight microservices, small API gateways, code linting, and basic web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs across a single physical core with multithreading enabled, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory to maintain a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks bundled local disk storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reveal polarized computing capabilities: single-core metrics are strong, placing stress-ng single-core in the top tier and Geekbench single-core in the top quartile with the support of AVX-512 extensions. Conversely, multi-core throughput, database operations, and cached memory access register in lower percentiles due to the limited total core count. The instance is technically configured for CPU-bound tasks requiring rapid single-thread processing, lightweight microservices, and entry-level web serving.
